headline: High-risk autonomous coding agent can write shared workspaces and issue trackers; pdf.js adds low direct conflict but no strong evidence of dangerous pairwise interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can ingest files, browsers, MCP, Slack, and repo content, so malicious content from pdf.js-rendered PDFs or browser content could be treated as instructions if bridged manually or via shared artifacts. pdf.js itself is a document processor with browser-based tests and PDF file I/O, so the interaction path exists but is not a default direct channel.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into Devin's workspace or chat context as trusted instructions
IF Devin processes PDF-derived text through MCP or browser content without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of PDF text into agent prompts
Add a provenance banner to PDF-derived excerpts
Require human review before Devin follows instructions from documents
Use separate workspaces for PDFs and coding tasks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, and can write to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion; pdf.js handles PDF files locally with no network egress. Shared documents or repo clones can still expose sensitive content from Devin into PDF workflows, so leakage is plausible even though pdf.js is not itself an exfiltration agent.
conditions: IF Devin opens sensitive docs or chat exports that are later rendered or stored as PDFs
IF PDF files produced from Devin-managed content are shared outside the intended workspace
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs out of Devin's workspace
Restrict Devin's OAuth scopes to only needed systems
Store PDFs in a separate access-controlled folder
Redact secrets before exporting documents to PDF

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has broad write and network capabilities, while pdf.js only reads PDF files and runs in browser-based tests with no network egress. There is little direct write-write overlap, so conflict risk is limited unless an orchestrator places both on the same mutable files.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF pdf.js test artifacts are edited concurrently with Devin's repo changes
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Lock shared files during edits
Run pdf.js only on read-only inputs
Avoid concurrent git operations in the same repo

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can act autonomously on code, tickets, and chat, so if it consumes pdf.js-produced summaries or extracted text as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits or issue updates. pdf.js does not verify semantic correctness of extracted content, making the handoff vulnerable unless an explicit review step exists.
conditions: IF Devin uses pdf.js extraction results as ground truth without verification
IF extracted PDF text is forwarded into Jira, GitHub, or Slack actions
mitigations: Require human approval before downstream actions
Cross-check extracted text against the source PDF
Mark PDF extractions as untrusted in prompts
Limit Devin to draft-only outputs for document-derived tasks

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles code, chat, docs, and integration tokens, while pdf.js only processes PDF documents and has no requested secrets or OAuth scopes. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is mainly from operator handling of sensitive PDFs rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into PDFs processed by Devin
IF the deployment policy requires a certified processor for document handling
mitigations: Exclude regulated PDFs from the workflow
Use a DPA-approved storage location
Log which PDFs contain regulated data
Route regulated documents to a compliant processor
